## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by small, flattened cells divided into two nearly symmetrical semicells by a deep central constriction. Euastrum denticulatum has trapezoidal semicells with distinct basal, lateral, and apical lobes, along with finely toothed margins and a prominent central swelling ornamented with small granules. It occurs primarily in slightly acidic, nutrient-poor to moderately nutrient-poor freshwater habitats, including ponds, wetlands, and shallow vegetated waters. Like many desmids, it is associated with relatively clear water and can serve as an indicator of freshwater habitat and water-quality conditions.
